short: Web3 URL to EVM Call Message Translation
introduction: ERC-4804 defines a standard translation of an HTTP-style web3:// URL into an EVM call message, so clients can read on-chain content through human-readable URLs instead of raw calldata. It was proposed by Qi Zhou, Chao Pi, and Sam Wilson in February 2022. The URL encodes a contract name or address, an optional chain id, a method, and arguments; a resolver parses these fields, resolves any name-service suffix such as .eth to an address, and builds a read-only view call whose returned data is shown as web content.
designPurpose: ERC-4804 was designed to remove the Web2 proxies that normally stand between users and on-chain data. Before it, reading a contract's content meant trusting a dApp website, a node provider, or a block explorer to translate a request into an EVM call, all outside the user's control. By fixing a URL grammar and a resolve-mode convention, ERC-4804 lets any client turn a web3:// URL directly into a view call, so on-chain HTML, SVG, and other resources can be fetched without a trusted intermediary.
commonUsage: The scheme is used to serve fully on-chain websites and media, where an address or ENS name plus a path maps to a contract method that returns HTML, SVG, or JSON. Browsers and gateways that understand web3:// resolve the name, choose the automatic or manual resolve mode, and display the result like an ordinary web page. It pairs naturally with ERC-5219, which formalizes the request-and-response contract interface that many web3:// resources implement.
sim.resolveUrlWalkthrough.name: Resolve a Web3 URL
sim.resolveUrlWalkthrough.desc: Follow a web3:// URL as a resolver parses it, resolves the name, builds an EVM call message, and returns the rendered content.
sim.resolveUrlWalkthrough.step.submit: The client submits a web3:// URL to a resolver that understands the scheme.
sim.resolveUrlWalkthrough.step.parse: The resolver parses the URL into its contract name, method, and arguments, then resolves the name to an address through the name service.
sim.resolveUrlWalkthrough.step.build: The resolver assembles an EVM call message, setting To to the resolved address and Calldata to the ABI-encoded method call.
sim.resolveUrlWalkthrough.step.call: The read-only view call runs on the target contract, and its returned bytes are rendered back in the client as web content.
